title: Per-lesson learning-objectives + entry-skill-floor front-matter schema (CI-linted)
context: PLAN.md v0.2 adds an explicit goal: anchor every lesson to per-lesson, measurable learning objectives (Bloom's-style 'the learner will be able to…') and a declared entry-skill floor ('never opened a terminal'), expressed as a CI-checkable front-matter block. This makes 'from zero' a spec, not an aspiration. The pedagogy review gate (§8) now requires these objectives to be present and CI-linted. This is an M0 exit criterion. It is distinct from skeleton-005 (which produces a module-level narrative skeleton) — this task defines the machine-readable schema embedded in every .qmd and the CI lint that enforces it.
objective: Define and implement the per-lesson learning-objectives + entry-skill-floor front-matter schema: a YAML front-matter block standard for every .qmd lesson, a JSON Schema or equivalent validator, and a CI lint step that fails the build if any lesson is missing or has a malformed learning-objectives or entry-skill block. Include an authoring guide (inline or in docs/) explaining Bloom's taxonomy verb selection and entry-skill floor values.
acceptanceCriteria: A committed schema document (e.g., schemas/lesson-frontmatter.schema.json or YAML Schema) defines required fields: at minimum 'learningObjectives' (list of Bloom's-style strings, ≥1), 'entrySkillFloor' (declared level, e.g. 'never-opened-terminal' | 'basic-terminal' | 'basic-R-or-Python'), and 'prerequisites' (list of lesson ids, may be empty).
A CI lint step validates every .qmd front-matter block against the schema and fails the build on any missing or malformed field.
An authoring guide (docs/lesson-authoring.md or inline in the schema doc) explains Bloom's taxonomy verb selection and the permitted entry-skill-floor values.
The pilot lesson (pilot-010) is updated to carry a conforming front-matter block as the reference example.
Reviewed by Pedagogy reviewer; schema/tooling licensed MIT, guide licensed CC-BY-4.0.
